turns.t: I'd rather not make a fuss, but my wife insisted. I've got a terrible pain in my left side, round the back.
You were right to come. Let's get you comfortable. When did the pain start?
About six this morning. It woke me up. I've not had a pain like it, to be honest.
How would you describe it? Constant, or does it come in waves?
Waves. It builds up until I can hardly stand, then eases off a bit, then builds up again.
How bad is it at the worst, if you had to put a word to it?
Severe. I was sick once on the way here, though I tried not to be in the car.
Does it spread anywhere, down into the groin for instance?
Yes, it goes round the front and down low. That's what frightened me.
Understood. Have you had a temperature or shivering? Any fever at all?
No fever. No shivers. Nothing like that.
Good. Now, what tablets do you take, if any?
Amlodipine, 5 mg, once a day. I take it in the morning with my tea.
And do you have any allergies, to medicines or anything else?
No, none that I know of. Never have.
Thank you. Is there any kidney trouble in your family? Your wife mentioned something on the phone.
My brother has polycystic kidney disease. That's why she was so worried when I called out.
That's useful to know. I'm going to check your numbers now, and then examine your back and tummy. ~
Right you are. ~
Pulse 96, blood pressure 148 over 90, temperature 36.8, oxygen 99 percent, and you're breathing 18 times a minute.
Is that bad? ~
Your pulse and pressure are a bit up, which is just the pain. The temperature is normal, which I like. Can you lean forward for me? ~
Ow. Yes. Careful, that's the spot. ~
You're very tender over the left loin, here, when I press. Your tummy itself is soft.
So what is it? Is it my kidney? ~
What you describe, with pain coming in waves and spreading to the groin, most likely a kidney stone. I'd like to be sure it's nothing more, though.
How do you do that? ~
I'd like to arrange a CT scan of your kidneys today. It's quick, and it shows a stone and whether your kidneys are blocked.
Today? Right. I thought I'd be sent home with a leaflet. ~
With the pain like this I'd rather see the picture first. I'll walk you round to radiology myself. ~
That's good of you. Can I have something for the pain? ~
I'll make sure the nurses see you straight away in the scan area. Please drink water while you wait, small sips.
Small sips. I'll do my best. ~
If the pain suddenly gets much worse, or you start shivering, tell the staff at once.
Understood. Thank you, doctor. My wife will be relieved. ~
Let's get you to the scan. Lean on me if you need to. ~

chief_complaint.value: a terrible pain in my left side

clinical_actions.description: Arrange CT kidneys, ureters and bladder
Advise small sips of water while waiting
